clue.text: Return draught container for fur

indicators.note: to return something is to send it back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a draught is a current of air
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: Someone is sending back a keg of beer and asking for a fur in exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draught container' looks like one thing, a beer barrel, but it splits into two pieces that are then turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name for the pelt of the coypu, a South American rodent, so a specific kind of fur.

clue.text: Go-it-alone politician brings about Italian result

indicators.note: 'about' signals the letters being turned around into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A maverick politician is credited with producing some result in Italy, perhaps an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings about' reads as 'causes', which glues the surface together; here it only tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts one-sidedly, without waiting for agreement from other parties or nations.

clue.text: I pester madly to get a welcome break

indicators.note: done madly, the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A child admits nagging frantically until they are finally allowed some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' sits after its fodder and reads as how the pestering was done, which hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a short rest from something difficult or unpleasant.

clue.text: Have I the skill to be pleasant?

blocks.note: recast 'have I' as the matching question built on the verb 'to be'
having the skill means being capable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are capable of being nice to people.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a question you rephrase rather than separate chunks: 'Have I the skill?' becomes 'Am I able?', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: friendly and good-natured in manner.

clue.text: Bird about to cut off banger

indicators.note: about = around, so the bird goes around the other piece

blocks.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family
to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: A bird is about to snip something off a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, and also for an old, clapped-out car, which is the sense wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional use: British 'banger' and American 'jalopy' both mean a battered old car.

clue.text: French man changing small to soft drink

indicators.note: changing one letter for another swaps S out and P in

blocks.note: Jules is a common French man's name
s = small, as on clothing labels
p = piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A Frenchman switches from something small to a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' looks like one phrase, but 'soft' is P and only 'drink' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a sweet drink, most famously the bourbon-and-mint version.

clue.text: Leans over sets of items

blocks.note: said of a ship tipping to one side in the water
items written one under another, like a shopping inventory

explanation.surface: Someone bends over collections of things, sorting through them.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical sense is the one to spot: a ship that lists leans over to port or starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a nautical verb for tilting, and the ordinary noun for itemised records.

clue.text: Politician and stiffly proper eastern cleric

blocks.note: prim = stiffly formal and proper
E = eastern
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A politician and a starchy churchman from the east are pictured side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleric' pulls toward church words, and the one it gives is also half the top political job.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the head of a parliamentary government is one particular politician.

clue.text: Greedy people are bound to get waste food

blocks.note: greedy eaters are called pigs
'they will' = they are bound to

explanation.surface: Gluttons are sure to end up eating leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a moral about gluttons; 'are bound to' has to be heard as a single verb of certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen scraps and leftovers fed to pigs, so waste food by its farmyard name.

clue.text: Roasting device tilts over

indicators.note: turned over, the word runs the other way

blocks.note: to tip is to tilt

explanation.surface: A rotisserie leans and falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' sits at the end and reads as 'falls over', but it is telling you to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which meat is turned over a fire to roast.

clue.text: Charge one, hail one

definitions.note: 'hail one' means 'one you hail', a noun phrase for the cab

blocks.note: a levy paid to the state
I = one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Two terse commands: bill someone, then flag someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves look parallel, but only the first is wordplay; the second is a playful definition of the thing you hail.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition: the thing you wave down from the kerb is a cab.

clue.text: Avoided being next to broken spades

indicators.note: broken into pieces and put back together differently

blocks.note: by = beside, next to
the six letters of SPADES, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone steered clear of standing beside some broken garden spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' reads as damaged garden tools, but it only tells you to rearrange the letters of the tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: going round something instead of through it is avoiding it.

clue.text: Take out permit entering river

indicators.note: one piece enters, going inside the other

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Britain
to let = to permit

explanation.surface: An order to remove a fishing licence that has strayed into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a noun, a licence, but it is the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to take out a word or file is to remove it.

clue.text: Animal gossip

blocks.note: a long-eared burrowing creature
British slang for chattering on, from rhyming slang where 'pork' rhymes with talk

explanation.surface: Talk about a creature, or a creature that talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The chatter sense is British slang: to rabbit on is to talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the burrowing animal, and a British slang verb for idle chatter.

clue.text: Trees to be represented on badge

indicators.note: to be re-presented is to be shown in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A design of trees is to appear on an emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' reads as grammar joining 'Trees' to 'be represented', but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a ribbon rosette is a badge worn as a prize or party emblem.

clue.text: Insect on stand is cause of annoyance

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: a bug is an insect
to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A bug perched on a display stand is irritating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a noun, a stand for things, but it is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a persistent source of irritation or dread.

clue.text: Spots the head's lack of caution

blocks.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
a ness is a headland, as in Sheerness

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the headteacher is being reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' suggests a headteacher; it is a geographical headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: acting hastily without thought is a lack of caution.

clue.text: Richie's single greeting

blocks.note: Lionel Richie's 1984 hit ballad, the one asking 'is it me you're looking for?'
the everyday word said on meeting someone

explanation.surface: A pop star's record doubles as a way of saying hi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like it means one of something, but it is a pop record; you need to know Lionel Richie's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a song title and the ordinary word of greeting.

clue.text: Discard, not initially, then throw out

blocks.note: to discard something is to turn it down
the first letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing out: first discard, then throw away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discard' and 'throw out' look like two halves of one instruction; the first is wordplay, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to throw someone out of a place is to expel them.

clue.text: Rock containing tip of fossil is plausible

indicators.note: the rock holds the other letter inside it
here the tip is the end of the word, its last letter

blocks.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, Gib for short
the end letter of fossiL

explanation.surface: A stone with a fossil in it is put forward as believable evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' wants to mean the first letter, F, but that gives nothing; it is the far tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Plausible in the slightly pejorative sense: smooth and fluent but shallow.

clue.text: Part of a clock is laid out

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters

explanation.surface: A clock component has been taken apart and set out on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' reads as a clock taken apart on a bench; 'out' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the numbered face of the clock is one part of it.

clue.text: Urgent request to dine in doorway

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: an entry is a doorway
to eat = to dine

explanation.surface: Someone at the door urgently asks to be fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a place to dine, but it says the eating goes inside the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an earnest, pleading appeal.

clue.text: To get furthest, just emboss it evenly

indicators.note: take the even-numbered letters: 2nd, 4th, 6th and so on

blocks.note: jUsT eMbOsS iT

explanation.surface: Advice for going the distance: just press it in smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evenly' reads as smoothly pressing, but it asks for letters 2, 4, 6 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: at the extreme limit, most distant.

clue.text: Timeless awful children making blunders

blocks.note: unruly children are little terrors
read it as time-less: T for time is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: Badly behaved kids keep messing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' looks like one word meaning eternal; split it as 'Time-less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: blunders are mistakes.
